Overview

Labuan as a Business Centre

Labuan is a federal territory of Malaysia covering about 92 square kilometres of islands off the coast of Sabah, with around 101,400 residents in late 2023. It has offered international business and financial services since 1990 through the Labuan International Business and Financial Centre (Labuan IBFC), regulated by the Labuan Financial Services Authority (Labuan FSA) under a separate body of law that includes the Labuan Companies Act 1990 and the Labuan Business Activity Tax Act 1990. More than half of the local workforce is employed in financial services, and the centre hosts banks, more than 230 insurers and intermediaries, money brokers and digital finance businesses. The island is also an offshore support hub for deepwater oil and gas, with supply bases, shipyards and fabrication yards.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Labuan mainly because Labuan entities appear in ownership chains, insurance programmes and financing structures across Asia. A counterparty may be a Labuan company whose shareholders sit elsewhere, a captive insurer or protected cell company may underwrite a group's risks, or a Labuan foundation or trust may hold assets that a creditor or claimant needs to reach. The regime's distinctive features, such as corporate directors, protected cells and transfer of domicile out of Labuan, can make control harder to see from public records. Oil and gas contractors on the island also raise conventional supply chain and integrity questions.

Typical Matters

Investigative Work Connected to Labuan

01

Ownership research on Labuan entities

Labuan companies can have corporate directors and shareholders in other jurisdictions, and some move domicile in or out with regulatory approval. We map directors, secretaries, related entities and the wider group from available filings, regulatory notices, litigation and open sources, and state clearly where control cannot be confirmed.

02

Insurance and captive counterparty diligence

Labuan hosts captive insurers, reinsurers and protected cell companies used by groups across Asia. We review licensing status, regulatory actions, principals and affiliates, and the claims and litigation history of a carrier or intermediary before reinsurance, fronting or distribution relationships are agreed.

03

Fintech and money broker screening

Digital asset businesses, money brokers and digital banks licensed in Labuan often market to customers outside Malaysia. We verify licences against the Labuan FSA's public information, identify the individuals behind the business and examine complaints, enforcement and adverse media in the markets where it operates.

04

Tracing assets in Labuan structures

Labuan foundations, trusts and holding companies may hold shares, vessels or investments for a debtor or defendant. Working with Malaysian counsel, we identify entities linked to the subject and connected service providers so counsel can assess disclosure applications, freezing relief or regulatory routes to beneficial ownership information.

05

Oil and gas contractor integrity

Operators and contractors using Labuan's supply bases, shipyards and fabrication yards rely on local subcontractors and agents. We review ownership, related parties, political exposure and enforcement history to support anti-bribery due diligence and contract decisions.

Local Context

Courts, Records and Institutions in Labuan

Labuan FSA and the Labuan regime

The Labuan Financial Services Authority, a statutory body headquartered on the island, licenses and supervises Labuan banks, insurers, trust companies, money brokers and other financial businesses and administers the registry for Labuan entities. Labuan entities are governed by their own statutes, including the Labuan Companies Act 1990, the Labuan Foundations Act 2010, the Labuan Trusts Act 1996 and the Labuan Business Activity Tax Act 1990, rather than the Companies Act 2016 that applies elsewhere in Malaysia.

Beneficial ownership reporting

Amendments to the Labuan Companies Act in 2022 strengthened the Authority's powers, including requiring beneficial owner information within seven days and striking off non-compliant companies, with penalties of up to 3 million ringgit. Labuan FSA guidance effective 1 July 2026 requires entities to submit beneficial ownership information through an appointed authorised agent, using a 25 percent threshold for companies, on incorporation, annually by 31 January and within 30 days of changes. The guidance does not make this information public.

Distinctive company law features

The Labuan Companies Act permits corporate directors, court-free amalgamations based on solvency declarations, transfer of domicile out of Labuan with Labuan FSA approval, and protected cell companies for specified insurance, captive and fund business. Each feature matters for investigations: corporate directors can obscure individuals in control, and redomiciliation can move an entity out of the register while its history remains relevant.

Courts and dispute resolution

Labuan falls within the jurisdiction of the High Court in Sabah and Sarawak rather than the High Court in Malaya, and disputes involving Labuan entities are frequently litigated in Kuala Lumpur, Singapore or other forums chosen in the contract. Applications for disclosure, winding up or preservation of assets concerning Labuan entities therefore need Malaysian counsel familiar with both court systems and the Labuan statutes.

Engagement Standard

How TDSC Scopes Matters in Labuan

TDSC has no office in Labuan and handles matters involving Labuan entities from Nashville. We begin by agreeing the purpose with the client and its Malaysian counsel, whether onboarding, reinsurance, investment, recovery or litigation, and identify which Labuan statute governs the entity. Research draws on Labuan FSA public information and registry filings obtainable through lawful channels, court records in Malaysia and other relevant jurisdictions, corporate records where the group's other entities sit, and open sources. We do not attempt to obtain confidential beneficial ownership submissions; where they matter, counsel considers court or regulatory routes. Any enquiries in Malaysia are carried out by professionals holding the required licences under Malaysian law.

TDSC has no office in Labuan. Engagements are directed from Nashville, Tennessee; where work on the ground is needed, it is performed by appropriately licensed local professionals under a written scope.

Questions

Labuan: Frequently Asked Questions

Can we find out who owns a Labuan company?

Sometimes. Labuan entities must report beneficial ownership to Labuan FSA, but the guidance does not make that information public. We work from available registry filings, directors and secretaries, connected entities in other jurisdictions, litigation and media. Where that is not enough, counsel may consider court orders or regulatory channels to obtain ownership information lawfully.

How do we check whether a Labuan financial business is licensed?

Labuan FSA publishes information on licensed entities, and we compare the claimed licence, name and activities against it, then look at principals, affiliates, complaints and enforcement in the markets where the business operates. Firms that use the Labuan name without a licence, or operate beyond their licence, are a recurring concern for investors and customers.

Why are Labuan structures relevant to asset recovery?

Labuan companies, foundations and trusts are used across Asia to hold shares, vessels, insurance interests and investments. A debtor may control assets through one without appearing in its public records. We identify links to the subject so counsel can decide whether to seek disclosure, freezing relief or recognition of a judgment in Malaysia.

Does a Labuan company's redomiciliation end the enquiry?

No. The Labuan Companies Act allows a Labuan company to transfer to another jurisdiction with Labuan FSA approval, and companies can also transfer in. We follow the entity to its new register, compare officers and filings before and after the move and treat the change itself as a fact to be explained.

Does TDSC have investigators in Labuan?

No. TDSC has no staff or licence in Malaysia. Most Labuan work is desk research from Nashville using lawful sources. Where enquiries on the ground are needed, they are carried out by Malaysian professionals licensed under the Private Agencies Act 1971, coordinated with Malaysian counsel.
